best_field_traits: Taxonomy caution: this project uses D. lindheimeri; many FNA/USDA sources treat the same concept as D. acuminatum var./subsp. lindheimeri. Do NOT create a duplicate card.
Basal rosette distinct in suitable season; upper stem leaves commonly 4–9 cm by 4–8 mm, often yellowish green.
Leaf surfaces and sheaths generally glabrous or sparsely hairy; conspicuous long papillose-based cilia near the blade base.
Ligule of hairs, often several millimeters long; compare actual collar, not just the nearby blade-margin cilia.
Open primary panicle about 3.5–7 cm; tiny often obtuse, obovoid spikelets about 1.3–1.6 mm.
Late-season stems develop many small leafy branch clusters (fascicles) and reduced secondary flowering heads.
crew_field_check: 1. Confirm original photo ROLE (flower macro, habitat view, or open panicle) before using a label; this image alone is NOT a verified same-plant key.
2. On living same-plant shoot find spring basal rosette and compare early spring versus late-season leafy secondary shoots.
3. Open the collar: photograph true hair-fringe ligule separately from hairs at the blade base, with mm scale.

4. Measure at least three mature ripe SPIKELETS with 1-mm ruler; size categories ~1.3–1.6 lindheimeri, 2.1–3.2 commutatum, ~2.9–4 oligosanthes, ~3–3.5 pedicellatum, but overlapping ranges prohibit pure size-only identification.
5. If rosette/collar/leaf base or mature spikelet dimensions unavailable, record Dichanthelium sp. and a source-determined tentative species.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: An individual intact labelled flowering Lindheimer panicgrass whole plant with rooted basal rosette and spring panicle
A 1.3–1.6 mm mature blunt spikelet with ruler, glumes and fertile lemma
Blade base papillae and long cilia separated from true collar hair ligule under 10–20×

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with D. oligosanthes (2.9–4 mm), pedicellatum (~3–3.5 mm) and commutatum (~2.1–3.2 mm), mature Lindheimer spikelets are substantially smaller. Confirm 1.3–1.6 mm with an actual scale and a true long hair-fringe ligule; open/airy panicle texture alone is not enough. The D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri source concept remains the same installed taxon.
comparisons.photo_context: Four real already archived source-labelled images are incorporated into a genus comparison. The Lindheimer habitat photo does not display a measured spikelet; none proves collar/leaf base anatomy. Morphological ranges are literature-based, not measured from these photographs.
not_reliable_alone: Airy panicle silhouette in a single season
Habitat or presumed annual/perennial condition from clipped stem
Ligule hair lengths or spikelet sizes inferred from photos without rulers
The older D. acuminatum var. lindheimeri name interpreted as a new separate species

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Rosette panicgrass — see photo evidence, then check the plant
steps: 1. Start with Cody Stricker's actual source-labelled open panicle close-up (photo 3): trace the fine flowering branches and see the small green oval spikelets. No millimeter scale or verified glume/lemma dissection is present.

2. Move to the second Cody Stricker photo (photo 4): examine the roots, narrow green blades, leafy shoots and dry basal sheaths. Roots are visible, but an individual rhizome, spring rosette and true ligule are NOT proven.
3. Use the original habitat photograph (photo 1) for field setting only. The grass is mixed with other plants and is not independently isolated as a species voucher.

4. Keep the historical Hitchcock–Chase plate (photo 2) as an explicitly separate illustration of an older Panicum lindheimeri name concept; do not substitute it for a photographed current-species diagnosis.

5. On a locally vouchered same plant, document spring basal rosette and later leafy shoots, a true hair-fringe ligule with 1-mm ruler, and at least three mature measured spikelets; inspect glumes and lemmas at 10–20×.
6. Compare same-stage D. commutatum, D. oligosanthes and D. pedicellatum. Published size ranges overlap; the two new close-ups are helpful orientation, not a final species certification.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Panicles often overlap. Show spring/autumn phase, true leaf collar, and at least three mature measured spikelets from the same plant before a firm species call.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Four real archived JPEG files confirmed by GitHub blob and JPEG signature checks (three field photographs, one historical illustration). Two Cody Stricker source-labelled photos were pixel-inspected and moved ahead of the old plate in the teaching sequence; their source page CC BY version could not be independently rechecked. No new JPEGs, fine anatomy arrows, or specimen-level identification certification. FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS and annotation_pending remain.
